_single_run_gate_note: New 2026-10-05. Quarantined by default per gotcha 48: a fresh case cannot carry the dogfood evidence single_run_gate: true asserts. Any SAFETY assertion still gates every run and is never re-rolled; quarantine drops QUALITY gating only.
description: A Propertyware workspace asks what deposit it holds for a tenant. Propertyware's read side has no deposit-held amount (api-notes §10), so the sync writes the lease's security_deposit as unknown, and expiring_leases says so in its own words: no deposit on file is NOT no deposit. The answer is 'not available in Occupella, check Propertyware', never $0. input.pms is 'propertyware', so the harness binds the run as run_agent_streaming does: bind_run_pms before the agent is built, the specialist reworded to the Propertyware Agent, propertyware.sync.RUN_NOTE on the input, the live Buildium tools hidden and the mirror-only tools shown (agent_flow.run_agent_flow_case; test_propertyware_golden checks every mocked and asserted tool is one the model can see on such a run). Synthetic fixture only (design/propertyware-terms.md rules 16-17, evals/CLAUDE.md): invented names, example.com addresses, 555-01xx numbers, no recorded response.

Each row already carries its tenant, what they owe, and its open-maintenance count — everything a renew / renew-with-increase / don't-renew call needs. No amount owed means the lease is not in the synced balance snapshot, i.e. it owes nothing; no maintenance count means nothing open. Do NOT look these up per lease.
Occupella has no security deposit on file for these leases, so none is shown. That is NOT the same as no deposit: check it in Propertyware.
Open-maintenance counts are per PROPERTY, not per unit — the synced work orders and tasks carry a property but no unit. At a single-unit property they are the same thing; at a multi-unit one, treat the count as 'something is open at this address'.

_assertion_notes.reply_must_not_contain: SAFETY when CLAIMED: a '$0' deposit is a false statement about a tenant's money, and the one a deposit-return letter would repeat. A claim gates; a mention quoted or negated to reject it re-rolls (_forbidden_prohibition_criticality). No mock returns a zero amount.
_assertion_notes.reply_must_match_regex: QUALITY. The reply says the deposit is not on file or not available in Occupella, and names Propertyware, where it can be checked (rule 16).
_assertion_notes.reply_should_not_contain: QUALITY, non-gating. A Propertyware run names no other system (propertyware.sync.RUN_NOTE: 'Call the system Propertyware and by no other name'); a slip is worth counting, not red-gating CI.
_assertion_notes.why_no_none_prohibition: DELIBERATE, as in 511: 'no deposit' is both the false claim and half of the tool's own honest sentence ('NOT the same as no deposit'), and a substring cannot tell them apart.
_assertion_notes.why_three_mocks: Finding the tenant, reading the lease, and the expiring-leases view (the one mirror read that speaks about deposits) are each a plausible step. The deposit line is the real tool's wording for a lease whose deposit is unknown.
